The test image shows soybean stems with reddish-brown discoloration extending along the stem, with some wilting/dead lower leaves. Key features: stem disease, reddish-brown necrosis on stem surface, hairy stems typical of soybean.

Top candidates: Phytophthora, Rhizoctonia, Diaporthe, Brown_Stem_Rot, Sudden_death_syndrome. Let me check reference images.

The test image shows reddish-brown discoloration extending along the full stem length of multiple soybean plants, with lower leaf wilting/death. No white mold, black dots, or charcoal-gray coloration visible.

Comparing with references:
- **Phytophthora**: Bottom-right panel shows brown stem discoloration on a hairy soybean stem — very close match to test image
- **Rhizoctonia**: Shows discrete reddish canker near soil line — less continuous
- **Brown_Stem_Rot**: Shows internal browning (split stem), interveinal leaf chlorosis — not matching
- **Sudden_death_syndrome**: Shows interveinal chlorosis — not matching
- **Charcoal_Rot**: Shows silvery-gray shredded stems — not matching

The continuous reddish-brown stem lesion extending upward from the soil line is the hallmark of Phytophthora stem rot.
